title: Reverse String
description: Given a string, reverse the order of its characters and return the reversed string.
input: A string containing characters that need to be reversed.
output: The input string with its characters arranged in reverse order.

examples.explanation: The characters of the string are arranged in reverse order.
The first character becomes the last character, the second becomes the second-last character, and so on.
The characters are reversed from their original order.

constraints: The input must be a valid string.

approaches.name: Using StringBuilder Reverse Method
approaches.description: Reverse the string using the built-in reverse() method provided by StringBuilder.
approaches.whenToUse: Use when built-in Java methods are allowed and the goal is to write concise and readable code.

approaches.name: Without Using Reverse Method
approaches.description: Reverse the string manually by iterating through its characters from the last index to the first index.
approaches.whenToUse: Use when built-in reverse methods are not allowed or when demonstrating string traversal and indexing logic in an interview.

interviewTips: Be prepared to solve the problem both with and without built-in methods.
Remember that String objects are immutable in Java.
Know the time and space complexity of each approach.
For manual reversal, understand why iteration starts from the last index.
